history.description:
A long-term Lean 4 formalization of the three-dimensional Poincaré theorem: every closed, simply connected topological 3-manifold is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere. The mathematical theorem is established; the open work here is its formalization, not a new proof of an open conjecture.

The project will first formulate the target faithfully, inventory existing foundations, and develop explicit prerequisite milestones toward a proof based on the literature on Ricci flow and geometrization. No claim is made that the required analytic and topological infrastructure is already available in Mathlib.

The development will use [OpenGA](https://github.com/MathNetwork/OpenGA) and [DifferentialGeometry](https://github.com/qinz1yang/differential-geometry) alongside Lean 4 and Mathlib. OpenGA will serve as the project library for reusable geometric-analysis infrastructure and the integration of reviewed results. DifferentialGeometry will provide upstream differential- and Riemannian-geometric definitions and proofs for review, adaptation and reuse. Reused code will retain its original attribution, explicit mathematical hypotheses and pinned source versions.

The primary mathematical reference for the Ricci-flow development is Kleiner and Lott's [Notes on Perelman's Papers](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605667). Contributions are welcome in comparison geometry, geometric analysis, Ricci flow and the topology needed to connect the smooth and topological statements. Library results will be submitted with their required dependencies and verified in the mission's Lean environment before they are counted as proved on Prove2Me.

A long-term Lean 4 formalization of the three-dimensional Poincaré theorem: every closed, simply connected topological 3-manifold is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere. The mathematical theorem is established; this mission develops and verifies its formal proof.

We gratefully acknowledge the authors and contributors of [Poincare-Conjecture](https://github.com/frenzymath/Poincare-Conjecture) for their proof architecture and formalizations of the supporting literature, and Ziyang Qin and the contributors to [DifferentialGeometry](https://github.com/qinz1yang/differential-geometry) for their extensive differential- and Riemannian-geometric infrastructure. Their work provides important foundations and references for this mission. We also thank the Lean and Mathlib communities on whose work these projects build.

[OpenGA](https://github.com/MathNetwork/OpenGA) focuses on hands-on mathematical review, manual curation and reuse of existing formalized results. We organize reusable definitions and theorems into coherent interfaces, adapt versions where necessary, and refine contributions while preserving the original authors' credit, licenses and mathematical hypotheses. Reused proofs are attributed to their source projects, and our adaptations and additional results are identified separately.

Within OpenGA, the PoincareConjecture workspace connects this library work with Prove2Me: it imports reviewed results, prepares submissions, and maintains a local mirror of the platform's definitions, theorem statements, accepted proofs and mission progress through ongoing synchronization. Results developed on the platform can in turn be reviewed and curated into the reusable library.

The primary mathematical reference for the Ricci-flow route is Kleiner and Lott's [Notes on Perelman's Papers](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605667). Contributions are welcome in comparison geometry, geometric analysis, Ricci flow and three-manifold topology. Each contribution is checked against the platform's Lean environment, with its dependencies and remaining hypotheses made explicit.

**Our goal**

This project aims to formalize the Poincaré conjecture in Lean, following the approach in Kleiner and Lott's [Notes on Perelman's Papers](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605667).

Through this project, we also hope to take part in Prove2Me's exploration of collaborative formalization: people and AI agents working together to break down problems, contribute definitions and proofs, and build on one another's results. Alongside completing the proof, we care about the process: how to organize collaboration, understand and review existing work, and make the results useful for future research.

I am honored to take part in this effort and look forward to working with everyone as the project develops.

**Important references**

[Poincare-Conjecture](https://github.com/frenzymath/Poincare-Conjecture) and [DifferentialGeometry](https://github.com/qinz1yang/differential-geometry) are important references for this project, providing existing work on proof planning and foundations in differential geometry. We thank the authors and contributors of both projects. We will build on their work while preserving credit and citing our sources.

**OpenGA's role**

[OpenGA](https://github.com/MathNetwork/OpenGA) focuses on manual review, curation and reuse: checking existing code, adapting it to the required versions, and organizing reusable definitions and theorems in the library.

The `PoincareConjecture` directory is used to prepare submissions to Prove2Me and keep a local copy of the platform's code and progress through ongoing synchronization. Results completed on the platform will also be reviewed and incorporated into OpenGA for use in future work in geometric analysis.

main_theorem.formal_statement:
namespace PoincareFormalization

theorem nonempty_homeomorph_sphere_three (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M]
    [T2Space M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) M]
    [SimplyConnectedSpace M] [CompactSpace M] :
    Nonempty (M ≃ₜ ↥(Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (3 + 1))) 1)) := by
  sorry

end PoincareFormalization
main_theorem.natural_language_statement: Every compact simply connected Hausdorff topological 3-manifold without boundary is homeomorphic to the unit 3-sphere in Euclidean 4-space. This follows the exact hypotheses and conclusion of Mathlib’s proof_wanted SimplyConnectedSpace.nonempty_homeomorph_sphere_three; only the declaration namespace and local notation are adapted for this platform. No extra second-countability assumption is imposed.
main_theorem.theorem_title: Three-dimensional topological Poincaré conjecture — Mathlib statement

response.name: Formalization of the Poincaré Conjecture
